properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-18 for Mission Bay's real-site pass: real, community-surveyed OpenStreetMap boundary (way 1329130170), the same pattern already used for Pier 70's Crane Cove Park (data/manual/pier70_crane_cove_park.geojson) -- not a hand trace or plan-diagram estimate. HIGH CONFIDENCE -- real, community-surveyed OSM polygon, independently confirmed via its Port of San Francisco operator tag and Wikidata id. Opened Oct 22, 2024 (5.4 acres at 16th St and Terry A. Francois Blvd, opposite Chase Center); occupies the plan's former P21/P22 open-space parcels (Mission Bay South Design Controls Plan Boundary/Block Map). 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: corrections to the description above. (1) The OSM way has no operator name tag and no Wikidata tag of its own; the only identifier is operator:wikidata=Q3398575 (the Port's item), so it is not 'confirmed via its Port operator tag and Wikidata id'. (2) 'Occupies the plan's former P21/P22 parcels' is not stated by any cited source (none mentions P21, P22 or the Design Controls Plan; Lotus Water says only 'P-22'); the owner should check the Design Controls Plan block map before this is restored.
properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- community-surveyed OSM polygon (way 1329130170). The way carries a website tag (sfport.com/bayfrontpark) and operator:wikidata=Q3398575 (the operator's Wikidata item, not the park's); it has no operator name tag or Wikidata tag of its own, so the confidence judgement is ours. Opened Oct 22, 2024 (5.4 acres at 16th St and Terry A. Francois Blvd, opposite Chase Center). Which plan parcels it occupies is not settled: Lotus Water's page calls it 'P-22'; that it also occupies P21 is not stated by any cited source (SF.gov notes a previously completed portion of Bayfront Park to the north).
properties.p_number: P22, 5.4 acres: Lotus Water's project page is titled 'Mission Bay Bayfront Park P-22' and describes a 5.4-acre site on the Mission Bay waterfront next to the Golden State Warriors arena (https://www.lotuswater.com/mission-bay-bayfront-park-p22). Lotus Water describes itself as a green-infrastructure and civil-engineering design firm, not as the park's landscape architect (SF.gov says the design was led by Mission Bay Development Group and Surfacedesign Inc.). Whether P21 is also part of the park is not established.
properties.notes: Opened Oct 22, 2024, per the SF.gov press release of that date; a public park to be owned and maintained by the Port of San Francisco (SF.gov).
